extracted.intended_audience: people attending live comedy shows / comedy club patrons
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for audience members on why they should not heckle during stand-up/comedy performances and how to behave if they dislike material. Focuses on preserving the show, respecting performers and other patrons.

rubrics_metrics.name: It's not helping
rubrics_metrics.description: The number one misconception is that shouted out (usually drunken) verbal abuse is somehow helpful to a comedian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heckling is not helpful or sought after. It doesn't make the show better and it's not showing anybody how clever you are. If you want to help, keep your comments to yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: It's not crowd work for the comic
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd work is crowd work. Heckling is heckling and never the two shall meet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crowd work will always be initiated by the comedian. If comedians want your opinion on a topic they will ask you. It is the comedian's job to start and control crowd interaction; uninvited shouting is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: It's not funny
rubrics_metrics.description: The heckler is never as funny as they think they are; it's an uninvited interruption that throws off timing and concentration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heckling can stop a great show in its tracks. While a comic's shutting down of a heckler can be funny, that reflects the comedian's skill, not the heckler being clever. Avoid interrupting the performer’s timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: The comic hates it
rubrics_metrics.description: Comics are good at dealing with hecklers because they have to be, not because they enjoy it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when a comedian appears to enjoy or skilfully handle a heckler, it's the result of years of dealing with rude comments. Heckling is something performers dislike and have to tolerate, not welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: It's flat out disrespectful
rubrics_metrics.description: Heckling is disrespectful to the comedian, the crowd and the venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some clubs have zero tolerance and may eject hecklers. Heckling can provoke other patrons (examples: beer dumped on a heckler's head, fistfights, security ejections). If you don't like a comedian's material, show disapproval with silence — an absence of laughter signals a wrong tack.
